A 51-year-old male patient presents with complaints of dizziness upon standing. He reports that the
symptoms started shortly after being diagnosed with hypertension and beginning treatment for it. He
has no other significant medical history. The physician decides to prescribe an alternative
antihypertensive medication that is less likely to cause orthostatic hypotension. Which of the following
is the most appropriate drug for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Enalapril (B) Methyldopa (C)
Prazosin (D) Clonidine (E) Doxazosin (F) Hydrochlorothiazide (G) Losartan (H) Verapamil (I)
Propanolol (J) Amlodipine
 A. Prazosin
B. Enalapril
C. Clonidine
D. Amlodipine
E. Hydrochlorothiazide
F. Verapamil
G. Losartan
H. Methyldopa
I. Doxazosin

J. Propanolol
